page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What sodium carbonate is
lines: anhydrous form is called soda ash.
It is made by the Solvay process.
steps.why: One compound is met here under three names — sodium carbonate, washing soda and soda ash — so the answer states the formula and says which name goes with which form before the uses begin.
common_mistakes: Writing NaHCO₃. That is sodium hydrogen carbonate, baking soda; sodium carbonate is Na₂CO₃.
Calling the anhydrous salt washing soda. Washing soda is the decahydrate, Na₂CO₃·10H₂O.
steps.memory_tip: Na₂CO₃ with ten waters is washing soda; the dry salt is soda ash.
steps.margin_note: Write the formula and both common names before listing the uses.

steps.label: Its uses
lines: 3. manufacture of glass, borax, soap and
4. in the paper, paint and textile
5. as a laboratory reagent in qualitative
steps.why: Water softening and cleaning are the household uses, glass, borax, soap and caustic soda are the manufacturing uses, and analysis is the laboratory use. Taking them in that order keeps the list from repeating itself.
common_mistakes: Giving the uses of caustic soda, such as refining petroleum. That belongs to NaOH.
Writing only that it is used in industry. Name the products made from it: glass, borax, soap, caustic soda.
steps.memory_tip: Home, then factory, then laboratory — the three kinds of use in order.
steps.margin_note: Some uses means a short list; four or five named uses is a comfortable length.

insider_note: Sodium carbonate and caustic soda are different compounds, Na₂CO₃ and NaOH, so open with the formula to show which one is being described.
